newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Westfield sees strong second half.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Westfield sees strong second half.

text.p: Shopping centre operator Westfield Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday that it expected the strong results achieved in the six months to December 31 to continue in the second half of the 1996/97 year.

Westfield reported a net profit of A$40.93 million for the six months to December 31, up from A$35.10 million a year earlier. "Directors expect the strong first half result to continue in the second half of the year," the company said.
Westfield said the 16.6 percent rise in net profit for the period maintained the company's continuous profit increases over its 37-year history as a public company.
Sales revenue rose 1.8 percent to A$275.1 million from A$270.2 million a year earlier.
Managing director David Lowy said all the group's key divisions contributed to the results.
Lowy said Westfield's strength and geographic diversity provided a sustainable basis for continuing earnings growth.
"We are confident about Westfield's future," Lowy said.

"We manage a portfolio of high quality shopping centres in Australia and the U.S., there is strong demand from retailers for existing and additional space, and we have extensive redevelopment plans to further improve these centres that meet demand," he said.
Lowy said U.S. activities, which have made an increasing contribution to profits in recent years, accounted for more than 50 percent of the operating profit during the period.

He said Australian businesses also continued to perform well during the period and that Westfield plans for a A$2 billion redevelopment plan in Austrlaia over the next five to seven years. "Feasibility studies had shown these projects would provide sound income and capital growth from the property owners - the Westfield Trust - and its joint venture partners," the company said.
Westfield shares were steady at A$19.80 at the midsession on Tuesday.
